perspective:
Bradley Ochoa’s available information:

- He works at a marketing firm as a salesperson with Katherine Lasiloo, a marketing manager/colleague. Their professional interactions concern disagreements and later collaboration over traditional sales methods versus digital marketing strategies.

- In a meeting room, he prepared data and charts from the last five campaigns to support traditional sales techniques. He tells Katherine he appreciates her digital strategies but believes core sales benefit more from traditional methods. He hears Katherine say she sees his point, but the market is evolving, digital outreach and online engagement matter, and they should analyze data together to integrate both approaches. He responds that he is not against digital marketing but is frustrated that proven methods are being sidelined without proper consideration.

- After the meeting, he hears/sees Katherine share recent digital campaign success stories that significantly boosted engagement and sales. He becomes uncertain about supporting only traditional methods. He asks Katherine to explain how these strategies are developed. He hears her explain targeting the right audience with the right message and offering to walk through analytics and decision-making. He admits his doubts and says the outcomes make him want to understand digital marketing more. He hears her say she is glad he is open, that adapting to market trends matters, and that they should dive deeper into the data.

- He proposes a joint strategy meeting, saying a combined approach could strengthen their campaigns. He hears Katherine agree, say combining strengths could lead to better results, and suggest scheduling a brainstorm/next-step session. He expresses hope that leveraging both their expertise can be impactful and thanks her for collaborating. He hears her say she looks forward to it and wants to leverage each other’s strengths.

- After a successful joint meeting, he feels excited and works overtime on a board presentation draft integrating both their ideas. He tells Katherine he has a draft and is excited. He hears her review it as comprehensive, well thought out, and reflective of his hard work. He says he is convinced the integrated approach will set them apart and wants to nail the presentation. He hears her say she is confident and suggests going through it again to fine-tune.

- After the presentation’s success and the new strategy’s implementation, he feels grateful for his professional growth and collaboration with Katherine. He tells her he learned much from her and is grateful. He hears her say it has been a pleasure, his openness made a successful partnership, and she values the collaboration. He proposes regular strategy sessions to continue momentum. He hears her call it a fantastic idea, say regular sessions will keep them on top of their game and market trends, and agree to do it.

He does not have access to Katherine’s private thoughts, personality type, race, education, or any narrator-only framing beyond what he directly observed, heard, or was told.
